text:
There was so rich a day last year...!

that now I do not even know what to do with it.


Severe mothers, guides to school,

besiege reflections, and we arrow

our faces barely. Only late to know

that in that mischief hinges

and the temple breaks.

What a day, that one last year,

that now I do not even know what to do with it,

the temple broken and everything.


For this they will separate us,

for that and so we will no longer do harm.

And the technical reflections still say,

will you not hear them?,

that inside two dark graph-lines and apart,

for having been children and also

for having joined too much in life,

they will lock us up, prisoners forever.


So that you may put yourself together.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem LXXIV - There Was So Rich a Day Last Year...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Vallejo's fractured school, childhood, and confinement imagery, including 'graph-lines' for gráfilas.
